# @cfast/email

> Send emails from Cloudflare Workers. Write them with react-email. Swap providers with a plugin.

## When to use
Use this package when you need to send transactional emails from Cloudflare Workers (or any edge runtime that cannot use SMTP). Templates are React components via react-email. Provider backends are pluggable.

## Key concepts
- **Workers-native**: Uses `fetch` and `FormData` instead of SMTP. No Node.js dependencies.
- **Lazy config**: Both `provider` and `from` accept getter functions called at send time, which is the Workers-friendly pattern for accessing env bindings not available at module scope.
- **React templates**: Email bodies are React components rendered to HTML and plain text via `@react-email/render`.
- **Pluggable providers**: Ships with Mailgun and a console (dev) provider. Custom providers implement a simple `{ name, send }` interface.

## API Reference

### Core (`@cfast/email`)

```typescript
function createEmailClient(config: EmailClientConfig): EmailClient;

type EmailClientConfig = {
  provider: EmailProvider | (() => EmailProvider);  // static or lazy getter
  from: string | (() => string);                    // default sender, static or lazy
};

type EmailClient = {
  send: (options: SendOptions) => Promise<{ id: string }>;
};

type SendOptions = {
  to: string;              // recipient address
  subject: string;         // email subject
  react: ReactElement;     // react-email component to render
  from?: string;           // override default sender for this message
};

type EmailMessage = {
  to: string;
  from: string;
  subject: string;
  html: string;   // rendered HTML
  text: string;   // rendered plain text
};

type EmailProvider = {
  name: string;
  send: (message: EmailMessage) => Promise<{ id: string }>;
};

class EmailDeliveryError extends Error {
  readonly provider: string;     // e.g. "mailgun"
  readonly statusCode?: number;  // HTTP status from provider API
  readonly response?: string;    // raw response body
  constructor(message: string, options: { provider: string; statusCode?: number; response?: string });
}
```

### Mailgun Provider (`@cfast/email/mailgun`)

```typescript
function mailgun(getConfig: () => { apiKey: string; domain: string }): EmailProvider;
```

### Console Provider (`@cfast/email/console`)

```typescript
function console(): EmailProvider;
// Logs email details to console. Returns { id: "console-{uuid}" }.
```

## Usage Examples

### Setup with Mailgun
```typescript
// app/email.server.ts
import { createEmailClient } from "@cfast/email";
import { mailgun } from "@cfast/email/mailgun";

export const email = createEmailClient({
  provider: mailgun(() => ({
    apiKey: env.get().MAILGUN_API_KEY,
    domain: env.get().MAILGUN_DOMAIN,
  })),
  from: () => `MyApp <noreply@${env.get().MAILGUN_DOMAIN}>`,
});
```

### Setup for development
```typescript
import { createEmailClient } from "@cfast/email";
import { console as consoleDev } from "@cfast/email/console";

export const email = createEmailClient({
  provider: consoleDev(),
  from: "Dev <dev@localhost>",
});
```

### Send an email
```typescript
import { email } from "~/email.server";
import { WelcomeEmail } from "~/email/templates/welcome";

await email.send({
  to: "user@example.com",
  subject: "Welcome to MyApp",
  react: <WelcomeEmail name="Daniel" />,
});
```

### Write a template
```tsx
import { Html, Head, Body, Text, Link } from "@react-email/components";

type WelcomeEmailProps = { name: string };

export function WelcomeEmail({ name }: WelcomeEmailProps) {
  return (
    <Html>
      <Head />
      <Body>
        <Text>Hi {name},</Text>
        <Text>Welcome to MyApp.</Text>
        <Link href="https://myapp.com/dashboard">Go to Dashboard</Link>
      </Body>
    </Html>
  );
}
```

### Error handling
```typescript
import { EmailDeliveryError } from "@cfast/email";

try {
  await email.send({ to, subject, react: <Template /> });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof EmailDeliveryError) {
    console.error(error.provider);   // "mailgun"
    console.error(error.statusCode); // 401
    console.error(error.response);   // "Unauthorized"
  }
}
```

### Custom provider
```typescript
import type { EmailProvider, EmailMessage } from "@cfast/email";
import { EmailDeliveryError } from "@cfast/email";

const myProvider: EmailProvider = {
  name: "my-provider",
  async send(message: EmailMessage): Promise<{ id: string }> {
    const res = await fetch("https://api.example.com/send", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },
      body: JSON.stringify(message),
    });
    if (!res.ok) {
      throw new EmailDeliveryError(await res.text(), {
        provider: "my-provider",
        statusCode: res.status,
        response: await res.text(),
      });
    }
    const data = await res.json();
    return { id: data.id };
  },
};
```

## Package exports
```
@cfast/email         -> createEmailClient, EmailDeliveryError, types
@cfast/email/mailgun -> mailgun
@cfast/email/console -> console
```

## Integration
- **@react-email/render**: Used internally to render React elements to HTML and plain text.
- **@react-email/components**: Use in templates for email-safe HTML structure (`Html`, `Head`, `Body`, `Text`, `Link`, etc.).
- **Cloudflare Workers**: Designed for Workers runtime. Config getters handle the lazy env binding pattern.

## Common Mistakes
- Passing static env values instead of getter functions. In Workers, env bindings are not available at module scope. Use `mailgun(() => ({ apiKey: env.get().KEY, ... }))` not `mailgun({ apiKey: env.KEY, ... })`.
- Importing `console` from `@cfast/email/console` shadows the global `console`. Use a renamed import: `import { console as consoleDev } from "@cfast/email/console"`.
- Not catching `EmailDeliveryError`. The client does not catch -- callers decide whether to fire-and-forget or handle errors.
- Using Node.js email libraries (nodemailer, etc.) alongside this package. This package is designed for edge runtimes without SMTP support.
